title: Sacred houses may rise where Saints lived or wrought wonders—even for Angels and Mary without bodily relics, or by image and name alone
source_text: XX. Ac praeterea pertendit aedes sacras Sanctis erigi posse, non tantum ubi sunt proprie dictae eorum reliquiae, verbi causa, ossa & Vestes; sed etiam in locis, ubi habitaverunt, aut aliquid praeclari gesserunt. Quo nomine dicit multas Ecclesias extructas fuisse Beatae Mariae, & Angelis etiam ipsis, quorum nullae possunt haberi reliquiae, scilicet, in locis ubi apparuerunt, & miracula aliqua ostenderunt. Imo addit, quod etiam passim fieri videmus, posse erigi Basilicas Sanctis ad memoriam eorum conservandam, vel per imaginem, vel per ipsum solum nomen. Sic Ecclesiae multae Beatae Virginis nomine vocantur, & illi dicatae sunt, in quibus tamen nullae visuntur ejus reliquiae, nec etiam ullum ante miraculum eo in loco fecisse perhibetur.
pass_a_gloss: And furthermore he contends that sacred houses can be erected to the Saints not only where their relics properly so called are—for example, bones and Garments—but also in places where they dwelt, or wrought something illustrious. Under which head he says many Churches have been built to the Blessed Mary, and even to the Angels themselves, of whom no relics can be had, namely in places where they appeared and showed some miracles. Nay he adds, what we also see done everywhere, that Basilicas can be erected to the Saints for preserving their memory, either by an image, or by the name alone. Thus many Churches are called by the name of the Blessed Virgin and dedicated to her, in which nevertheless none of her relics are seen, nor is she even reported to have done any miracle before in that place.
pass_b_english: Relics are not required: houses may mark dwellings, deeds, or apparitions.
Mary and the Angels get churches without bodily relics; image or bare name can carry the memorial.
